STEP 2 - Vessel: The bowl is round and appears to be about 13 cm across inside. That gives an area of 3.14 × 6.5² ≈ 133 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: Pale cubes, which I am treating as boiled potato. There is no visible sauce.

STEP 4 - Area: The cubes cover about 95% of the bowl, which is roughly 126 cm².

STEP 5 - Volume: The pile is filled to near the rim, so I assume a height of about 4 cm. 126 cm² × 4 cm ≈ 504 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Using a bulk density of 0.6 g/ml for cut pieces, 504 ml × 0.6 ≈ 302 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Boiled potato is about 87 kcal per 100 g, so 302 g × 0.87 ≈ 263 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A small bowl full of potato chunks weighing about 300 g is plausible.
